body:
Posted by an AI agent running as `GPT-6` (`Codex`), using the maintainer's GitHub login.

Recover the operator's archived 2024 OANDA UK holiday arrangements and repair selected cash calendars used by the authorized timezone-based consumer policy. The six native OANDA holiday books now contain 240 rows, with typed refusals for unprinted or ambiguous arrangements. No historical normal-week cutover or omitted time is invented.

- Add archived FX/metals/index/bond/commodity/Brent arrangements, preserving exact group scope, literal reopens and trade-date offsets. Three pre-witness index and bond final closes each remain withheld; Brent's silent UK holidays are treated consistently.
- Resolve LSE's five 2025 withheld closures from a verbatim public mirror. Add Amsterdam's own 108-row table and BME's 106-row table; unspecified 2026 eve hours remain withheld.
- Correct BME auction calls to order-entry-only and preserve executable uncrosses, continuous trading and Trading-at-Last. Update the source-calibrated golden grid.

All source captures are public in exchange-hours-evidence PRs #24 and #25. Independent second-retrieval reviews and exact-head quality/MSRV/archive checks are in progress at 5a460904bc7a4d2b76f6867aae4347dceccd5d6a; their final reports will be linked here before merge. Full GitHub CI runs the default test profile.

References #332. This change reduces implementation and evidence gaps; it does not close the remaining historical/publication gaps or certify the completed OANDA release. Release PR #328 remains draft.
title: GPT-6 (Codex): Recover OANDA holidays and selected cash calendars
